items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1967-10-28
items.q: I used to go up there quite a bit... Duke Ellington still had a banjo on the band.

ctx.x: outshine him, even with the five and the seven, you know, the high five and the seven. Well, he was playing so much at that time, I don't see how anybody could have. He was so far. Yeah, he was 20 years ago. He sounded about as good on that thing, starting with some barbecue as you've ever heard him. Let's take this. Well, I was glad the minute I heard that, I figured it was that band because I was so familiar with that band. I played a lot of vaudzo myself with a fellow

by the name of Jack Pettis, and we used to run across Louis every once in a while, you know. Let's take one more break here, and then we'll come back and listen to some more from that album, and also some old Duke Ellington that's kind of interesting. We'll be back on jazz review after this word. Now, a few words about the Sony 250A tape deck. Forget it. Forget about leaving it on. items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1959-07-16
items.q: I seen him in California. We were making a date the same time as Ellington was making a date in California. I seen him keep Ellington from 8 o'clock in the morning until 6 o'clock at night without making a side.

ctx.x: Who made the records? Do you know?

Yeah. The ones they made here, you mean? Uh, uh... August Schillang on drums. Uh... Santo, Rap. Well now they made... They made two sessions here. They made an OK session here and they made a Victor session here. The OK was with Santo, Rap, Paul... Steve Loiskaner, Freddie Newman, piano, and Chink. And a tenor? Lester. Lester Bouchon. Yeah. And the drums? August Schillang. Yeah. The Victor date, it started out with the same band, but Rap, Old Man King was the recording you used. You ought to know about him…
